SubmissionView : list_acl

SubmissionView_ListAcl.Rd

List the Access Control Lists (ACLs) for this entity and optionally its children.

This function returns the local sharing settings for the entity and optionally its children. It provides a mapping of all ACLs for the given container/entity.

Important Note: This function returns the LOCAL sharing settings only, not the effective permissions that each Synapse User ID/Team has on the entities. More permissive permissions could be granted via a Team that the user has access to that has permissions on the entity, or through inheritance from parent entities.

Usage

synListAcl(instance, recursive=FALSE, include_container_content=FALSE, target_entity_types=NULL, log_tree=FALSE, synapse_client=NULL)

Arguments

instance

(SubmissionView) The SubmissionView instance to operate on.

recursive

(bool) If TRUE and the entity is a container (e.g., Project or Folder), recursively process child containers. Note that this must be used with include_container_content=TRUE to have any effect. Setting recursive=TRUE with include_container_content=FALSE will raise an error. Only works on classes that support the synSyncFromSynapse() function.

include_container_content

(bool) If TRUE, include ACLs from contents directly within containers (files and folders inside self). This must be set to TRUE for recursive to have any effect. Defaults to FALSE.

target_entity_types

(Optional[list[str]]) Specify which entity types to process when listing ACLs. Allowed values are "folder", "file", "project", "table", "entityview", "materializedview", "virtualtable", "dataset", "datasetcollection", "submissionview" (case-insensitive). If NULL, defaults to list("folder", "file").

log_tree

(bool) If TRUE, logs the ACL results to console in ASCII tree format showing entity hierarchies and their ACL permissions in a tree-like structure. Defaults to FALSE.

synapse_client

(Optional[Synapse]) If not passed in, the last created instance from the Synapse class constructor will be used.

Value

An AclListResult object containing a structured representation of ACLs where: - entity_acls: A list of EntityAcl objects, each representing one entity's ACL
- Each EntityAcl contains acl_entries (a list of AclEntry objects)
- Each AclEntry contains the principal_id and their list of permissions

Errors

- An error is raised if the entity does not have an ID or if an invalid entity type is provided.
- An error is also raised if there are permission issues accessing ACLs.
- An error may also be raised for any other issues that occur during the process.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
## Example 1: List ACLs for a single entity
    library(synapser)
    synLogin()

    acl_result = SubmissionView(id = "syn123") |> synListAcl()
    acl_result

    # Access entity ACLs (entity_acls is a list, not a named list)
    for (entity_acl in acl_result$all_entity_acls) {
        if (entity_acl$entity_id == "syn123") {
            # Access individual ACL entries
            for (acl_entry in entity_acl$acl_entries) {
                if (acl_entry$principal_id == "273948") {
                    cat(sprintf("Principal 273948 has permissions: %s\n", acl_entry$permissions))
                }
            }
        }
    }

    # I can also access the ACL for the file itself
    acl_result$entity_acl

    acl_result

## Example 2: List ACLs recursively for a folder and all its children
    library(synapser)
    synLogin()

    acl_result = Folder(id = "syn123") |> synListAcl(
        recursive = TRUE,
        include_container_content = TRUE
    )

    # Access each entity's ACL (entity_acls is a list)
    for (entity_acl in acl_result$all_entity_acls) {
        cat(sprintf("Entity %s has ACL with %d principals\n", entity_acl$entity_id, length(entity_acl$acl_entries)))
    }

    # I can also access the ACL for the folder itself
    acl_result$entity_acl

    # List ACLs for only folder entities
    folder_acl_result = Folder(id = "syn123") |> synListAcl(
        recursive = TRUE,
        include_container_content = TRUE,
        target_entity_types = list("folder")
    )

    # List ACLs for specific entity types (e.g., tables and views)
    table_view_acl_result = Folder(id = "syn123") |> synListAcl(
        recursive = TRUE,
        include_container_content = TRUE,
        target_entity_types = list("table", "entityview", "materializedview")
    )

## Example 3: List ACLs with ASCII tree visualization
    # When log_tree = TRUE, the ACLs will be logged in a tree format. Additionally,
    # the ascii_tree attribute of the AclListResult will contain the ASCII tree
    # representation of the ACLs.
    library(synapser)
    synLogin()

    acl_result = Folder(id = "syn123") |> synListAcl(
        recursive = TRUE,
        include_container_content = TRUE,
        log_tree = TRUE # Enable ASCII tree logging
    )

    # The ASCII tree representation of the ACLs will also be available
    # in acl_result$ascii_tree
    acl_result$ascii_tree
} # }
